To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Antibiotic residues present in human cardiovascular tissues after decontamination with bank-prepared antibiotic cocktails may mask microbial contamination, resulting in falsely negative microbiological analyses."

antibiotics used for decontamination of human cardiovascular tissues may remain present in tissues after cryopreservation and processing, and may affect the results of standard microbiological analyses.

(a) antibiotics present in cryopreserved tissues and cryoprotection media after decontamination can interfere with microbiological analyses; (b) the RESEP tube method is a simple, inexpensive and effective way to remove residual antibiotics from cryopreserved tissues, and (c) the presence of antibiotics may result in falsely negative microbiological analyses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the risk of false negative microbiological analyses in cryopreserved tissues, due to the presence of antibiotics.
the risk of falsely negative results for microbial contamination of cryopreserved human cardiovascular allografts, due to residual antibiotics.
the presence of antibiotics, which are used for tissue decontamination, in cryopreserved tissues, and their potential interference with microbiological testing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although the microbiological analysis performed in the tissue bank is negative, the tissue could contain residual antibiotics, and thus, the presence of bacteria and/or fungi cannot be excluded.

the presence of antibiotics after decontamination of human cardiovascular tissues intended for transplantation, may mask the presence of microorganisms in the samples and may result in false negative microbiological results.
the use of antibiotics in the decontamination process of cardiovascular tissue allograft should be avoided or at least the presence of antibiotics must be checked before microbiological analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antibiotics in cryopreservation media may mask microbial contamination of cryopreserved tissues during microbiological testing.
antibiotic residues present in decontaminated tissue allograft and processing liquids may mask microbial contamination and result in false negatives.

the presence of antibiotics after decontamination can lead to a falsely negative result in the standard microbiological analysis, and the RESEP tube can be used for removal of antibiotic residues in cryopreserved tissue before microbiological analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of antibiotics may mask the presence of bacteria and fungi in cryopreserved tissue allograft samples.

the presence of residual antibiotics in cryopreservated cardiovascular tissues intended for transplantation may lead to false negatives during microbiological analysis, and may be a source of infection in transplant recipients.
microbiological analyses performed on tissues after cryopreservation should include a RESEP treatment, in order to avoid false negative results.
